themes_detail.label: Dead Animal Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Dead animals are being reported at 17 complaints THIS WEEK—an 850% surge above the 2.0 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—suggesting either a disease outbreak, pest infestation, or environmental hazard requiring immediate public health investigation.
evidence: 17 dead animal complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (750% spike, z-score 6.71)
Spike is acute and concentrated in a single week, not gradual trend
High statistical significance indicates anomalous event rather than seasonal variation
reporting_angles: Interview Department of Health & Mental Hygiene and NYPD Animal Care & Control about possible disease vectors or environmental contamination in Bay Ridge/Dyker Heights
Canvass affected blocks to identify geographic clustering and whether residents have noticed sick wildlife or other signs of ecological distress

themes_detail.label: Electrical System Failures Spike
themes_detail.summary: Electrical complaints jumped to 15 THIS WEEK versus a 4.1 weekly baseline—a 266% spike with z-score 7.98—raising questions about aging grid infrastructure, meter problems, or coordinated service disruptions in CD 310.
evidence: 15 electrical complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (264% increase, z-score 7.98)
Represents sharp one-week spike, not gradual increase
Electrical infrastructure issues correlate with aging housing stock (374 alterations filed in last 90 days suggest renovation pressure)
reporting_angles: Contact Con Edison to determine whether specific substations or transformer banks are experiencing failures or overloads in Bay Ridge/Dyker Heights
Interview residents about power outages, brownouts, or electrical hazards they've experienced this week

themes_detail.label: Animal in Park Surge
themes_detail.summary: Parks complaints involving animals spiked to 5 THIS WEEK from a 0.4 weekly average—a 1,150% increase with z-score 9.55—suggesting possible wildlife encroachment, loose pets, or park safety concerns that warrant ecosystem investigation.
evidence: 5 animal-in-park complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1,233% spike, z-score 9.55)
Coincides with dead animal spike, suggesting possible disease or ecological imbalance
Parks department reconstruction/upgrade is standing budget request, indicating long-running maintenance issues
reporting_angles: Contact Parks Department to identify which Bay Ridge/Dyker Heights parks are affected and what animals have been reported
Investigate whether animal spike correlates with dead animal complaints—possible rabies, distemper, or other wildlife disease outbreak

themes_detail.label: Illegal Fireworks Enforcement Gap
themes_detail.summary: Illegal fireworks complaints rose to 9 LAST WEEK from a 0.8 weekly baseline—an 1,025% increase with z-score 7.57—indicating either organized illegal activity or enforcement lapses during a critical week.
evidence: 9 illegal fireworks complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1,100% increase, z-score 7.57)
Spike is isolated to single week, suggesting acute event or coordinated activity
Noise complaints (690 over 90 days) suggest ongoing quality-of-life issues; fireworks spike may represent escalation
reporting_angles: Interview NYPD about enforcement actions and whether there's organized illegal fireworks sales or distribution in Bay Ridge/Dyker Heights
Canvass residents about when/where fireworks were heard and whether this correlates with specific date (July 4th weekend, other holiday) or criminal enterprise

themes_detail.label: Building/Use Violations Surge
themes_detail.summary: Building/use complaints exploded to 66 complaints 2 WEEKS AGO from a 9.4 weekly baseline—a 604% spike with z-score 15.01, the highest statistical severity—suggesting widespread zoning violations, illegal conversions, or unlicensed commercial activity that warrants DOB investigation.
evidence: 66 building/use complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 9.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (604% spike, z-score 15.01—highest severity)
Active ULURP rezonings at 9201 4th Ave and 9818 Fort Hamilton Parkway may indicate zoning enforcement pressure or illegal pre-development activity
443 permit filings in last 90 days (374 alterations) suggest high volume of construction; spike may indicate unlicensed or non-compliant work
reporting_angles: File FOIL request to Department of Buildings for details on the 66 complaints: what types of violations, which buildings, what enforcement actions taken
Interview CB 310 leadership and elected officials about whether they've flagged building/use problems; cross-reference with ULURP rezoning activity
Investigate whether illegal residential conversions, unlicensed day cares, or other unsafe occupancy changes are driving the spike
